metadata.title: Above Avalon: Trump Reinstates Jensen Huang as NVIDIA CEO

content.text:
Hello everyone.
We need to continue our discussion regarding how Apple can respond to digital search behavior changing because of AI. The plan is to do that tomorrow. Today’s update will be focused on one of the more remarkable business news stories.
Let’s jump in.
Trump Reinstates Jensen Huang as NVIDIA CEO
It’s well beyond time to batten down the hatches in preparation of what is to come.
In a move that lacks any parallel in modern business, President Trump personally intervened to force NVIDIA’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO effective immediately.
Shortly after the news was announced earlier today before market open, Trump went on CNBC to confirm his direct involvement in Huang’s reinstatement. Trump’s 51-minute interview can be viewed/listened to here. The interview was a wild ride.
In hindsight, Treasury Secretary Bessent’s dramatic about-face over the weekend regarding both NVIDIA and Jensen Huang was a clue that something was up. Yesterday, Bessent went on CBS to say that it may make sense for NVIDIA to have Huang back as CEO. Bessent had previously said NVIDIA needed to move on from Huang.
Here’s the beginning of NVIDIA’s press release announcing Huang’s reinstatement:
“NVIDIA today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.
‘The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,’ said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board.”
